INC-86  Dangerous-goods check lets explosives sit next to oxidisers
status: open   priority: P1   area: stowage   reported: 2026-08-14 by stowage-planning

A class 1 container was planned directly beside an oxidiser and the stowage check raised
nothing. It looks like any hazard class written with a division, such as oxidisers or
organic peroxides, is never matched against the segregation table.

Acceptance:
  mustSegregate("1", "5.1"), mustSegregate("5.1", "1"), mustSegregate("2.1", "5.1") and
  mustSegregate("5.2", "3") are all true; mustSegregate("3", "8") and mustSegregate("8",
  "5.1") stay false; adjacentConflicts reports such pairs.

  src/cargo/hazmat.ts

content.text: All tests pass. The bug was in `primaryClass` in `src/cargo/hazmat.ts:13-15`, which stripped everything after the "." for every hazard class, collapsing distinct hazard classes like `5.1` (oxidiser) and `5.2` (organic peroxide) down to `"5"` — a value that doesn't exist in the segregation table, so those pairs were silently treated as safe. Only class 1 (explosives, divisions 1.1–1.6) is actually a single hazard identity split by division; other classes' divisions are distinct hazards. Fixed by only stripping the division for class 1, and updated/expanded tests to cover the acceptance criteria in INC-86.
